Subject: MAP & evaluation plan — proposed rebaseline

Hi Asha / procurement team,

Following our call this morning I wanted to document an updated mutual action plan and suggest a rebaseline for the close timeline. Procurement flagged a vendor review window that pushes their legal/IT sign-off into the week of May 24, which would affect the previously targeted May 21 close.

Quick summary:
- Current close date: 2027-05-21
- Proposed new close date: 2027-06-04 (two-week buffer to allow procurement + SOC evidence review)
- Key evaluation milestones to shift:
  - Sandbox access: was 5/12 -> proposed 5/19
  - E2E eval (clinical workflows): was 5/17 -> proposed 5/26
  - Legal sign-off: was 5/20 -> proposed 5/28

If Nimbus is comfortable with the 6/4 close, Redwood can commit to:
1) Reserved sandbox environment and a prioritized onboarding engineer for the 5/19 sandbox handoff.
2) A condensed evaluation kit (we'll focus on the 3 top-priority prompts and telemetry to shorten the E2E window).
3) A documented rollback/fallback plan in case procurement needs an additional week (we'll keep the original pricing and credits window for 10 business days after 6/4).

I've attached the current MAP (Nimbus_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short procurement schedule (procurement-schedule.pdf). Please confirm whether your team can accept the new dates or if you prefer a different cadence.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0187

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the note and clear options. Procurement confirmed the vendor review board is booked the week of May 24; legal will only be able to start redlines after that meeting. Given that, a 2-week shift to 6/4 sounds reasonable. A couple of asks from our side:

- Can Redwood guarantee sandbox credentials for the 5/19 handoff? The review team wants a hard date so they can sync internal testers.
- On the evaluation kit: can you highlight the three priority prompts and the minimum telemetry you need so we can prep data ahead of time?

I cc'd procurement (procurement@nimbushealth.com) to keep them in the loop. If we hit any further delays on our side we'll flag it, but we intend to target 6/4.
